title: Randomized Controlled Trial Assessing the Effectiveness and Safety of Fecal Microbiota Transfer for VRE Eradication in Immunocompromised Patients – VRE-ex
official: Randomized Controlled Trial Assessing the Effectiveness and Safety of Fecal Microbiota Transfer for VRE Eradication in Immunocompromised Patients (EU CTR, Phase II) – VRE-ex
summary: Main objective: To assess the rate of VRE decolonization in immuncompromised patients in comparison to placebo.

interventions.name:
MOVIPREP®,
Pulver zur Herstellung einer Lösung zum Einnehmen

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adult patients (≥18 years)
2. Confirmation of known intestinal VRE colonization defined as presence and growth of VRE in a fecal sample within 1 week prior to randomization
3. Patients at risk of VRE infection due to one of the following oncological therapies: Scheduled for allogeneic or autologous stem cell transplantation or CAR-T cell therapy in four to eight weeks following FMT or Patients currently undergoing immune-checkpoint inhibitor therapy or treatment with bispecific antibodies with at least one more treatment planned within the consecutive eight weeks
4. Written informed consent and data protection declaration obtained prior to the initiation of any protocol required procedures
5. Willing and able to comply to study procedures and study protocol
Exclusion criteria:
1. Ongoing or planned antibiotic treatment or prophylaxis within 30 days of first treatment visit (d0) excluding co-trimoxazole
2. Current hospitalization in an Intensive Care Unit
3. Current pregnancy or nursing period
4. Woman of childbearing potential not willing to use an acceptable highly effective contraception method (failure rate of < 1% per year) from screening visit until at least 30 days after last IMP administration; otherwise the participant needs to agree abstaining from heterosexual intercourse during the study and this needs to be acceptable in relation to the preferred and usual lifestyle of the participants in the discretion of the investigator
5. Other conditions that according to the investigator might interfere with the evaluation of study objectives or patient safety.
6. Patients who are institutionalized by court order or regulatory action
7. Patients, who are members of the staff of the study site, staff of the sponsor or involved Clinical Research Organisation (CRO), the investigator him-/herself or close relatives of the investigator
8. Legal incapacity and/or other circumstances rendering the patient unable to understand the nature, scope and possible impact of the clinical trial
9. Planned initiation of antimicrobials other than IMP with the purpose of VRE eradication during the study period
10. Foreseeable inability to swallow 30 FMT capsules within 5 hours on two days each
11. Uncontrolled inflammatory bowel disease (e.g. ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease) defined as the necessity to start or modify immunosuppressive treatment within the preceding three months due to disease activity.
12. Presence of severe intestinal inflammation due to other cause
13. Advanced stage chronic heart failure (NYHA III/IV)
14. Gastrointestinal perforation, obstruction, ileus or retention of gastric contents
15. Concomitant participation in another interventional clinical trial
16. Known hypersensitivity or allergy to any of the components of the study treatment
